chunks: And from him, from Hammad ibn Isa, and Fadalah, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the Mutamatti' (one who performs Hajj al-Tamattu'), when does he visit the House? He said: 'On the Day of Nahr (10th of Dhul-Hijjah) or the next day, and he does not delay.' And the Mufrid and the Qarin are not equal; they are given ease (to delay). This also indicates that it is permissible for the Qarin and the Mufrid until the third day and more than that, as narrated:

key_terms.الْقَارِن: One who performs Hajj al-Qiran (combining Umrah and Hajj together)
key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّع: One who performs Hajj al-Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj with a break)
key_terms.الْمُفْرِد: One who performs Hajj al-Mufrid (Hajj only, without Umrah)
key_terms.يَزُورُ الْبَيْتَ: Visits the House (referring to Tawaf al-Ifadah)
key_terms.يَوْمَ النَّحْرِ: The Day of Sacrifice (10th of Dhul-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: When should a Mutamatti' pilgrim perform Tawaf al-Ifadah during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinct rulings for Tawaf al-Ifadah, emphasizing the urgency for the Mutamatti' to perform it immediately after Eid al-Adha, while granting the Mufrid and Qarin a broader window until the 13th of Dhul-Hijjah. This distinction highlights the jurisprudential nuance in Shia fiqh regarding the completion of Hajj rites based on the specific type of pilgrimage performed. The narration underscores the practical application of prophetic traditions in structuring the pilgrimage calendar for Shia Muslims.
